findings.evidenceJa: 倒れ伏したセイバーだけ
findings.governingReading: Only Saber remains there, collapsed after the sword vanishes.
findings.explanation: The English omits her fallen posture, weakening the immediate visual evidence that drives Shirou toward her.

findings.highlight: her breathing is weak yet irregular
findings.evidenceJa: 呼吸は弱々しいクセに激しく
findings.governingReading: Saber’s breathing is weak yet violent or rapid, as if she is delirious with fever.
findings.explanation: Irregular invents a rhythm and again removes the paradoxical intensity of breaths too weak to sustain her.

findings.governingReading: Shirou recoils with an exclamation that her forehead is hot.
findings.explanation: Ow recasts his recognition of abnormal heat as a generic cry of pain.

findings.highlight: her only reply is heavy breathing
findings.governingReading: Only Saber’s suffering, labored breathing answers Shirou.
findings.explanation: Heavy describes effort but again removes the explicitly painful quality of her condition.

findings.governingReading: Shirou tells Saber that they will be home soon and orders her to remain still until then.
findings.explanation: The English makes Shirou alone the subject of going home and turns expected arrival into an immediate departure statement, blurring that he is already carrying her there.

findings.evidenceJa: セイバーの姿だけだった
findings.governingReading: The only thing left is the sight of Saber in Shirou’s arms, letting out painful breaths.
findings.explanation: The English replaces the visible image that closes the scene with Shirou’s vague sensation and weakens Saber’s suffering into what he feels.
